suspicious_changes: Bus operator reassignment: agency_id changed from 202 (SBS Transit Ltd) to 201 (Go-Ahead Singapore) for 29 of 642 routes (4.5%) — e.g. SB_10, SB_18, SB_19, SB_20, SB_23, SB_28, SB_29... No route_id, route_short_name, or trip content changed for these routes, only the operating agency. Consistent with a bus-package contract handover (LTA periodically re-tenders operating packages) rather than a data error, but material enough (nearly 1 in 20 routes) to flag for confirmation.

Circle Line Extension (route 'CE') fully retired and replaced: route CE (1,030 trips) removed along with its two stops (CE1, CE2) and the 6 transfers.txt rows referencing them; one new route (TTS_461, 'Yishun East - Khatib MRT', 30 trips, operated by Tower Transit) added. The nearby interchange stops CC15/NS17/NS17_CC15 shifted 52.0m in the same update. All references were removed together (no orphaned route_id/stop_id left behind, verified against trips.txt), so this reads as a real, internally-consistent network restructuring around the Circle Line Extension — not a broken diff — but the scope (a full line retired) warrants a human sanity-check against MRT network announcements.

checks_passed.new_validator_warnings: None — same 4 notice codes in both feeds, same counts and severities. Caveat: both hosted reports (gtfs-validator 8.0.1) show ERROR-severity invalid_input_files_in_subfolder / missing_calendar_and_calendar_date_files / missing_required_file because the source zips nest all GTFS files one directory level down (e.g. Singapore_SINGAPORE_MAPKING_20260630-000/) instead of at the zip root — the validator can't find calendar.txt, stops.txt, routes.txt, trips.txt, stop_times.txt, agency.txt at the top level, so it never reaches row-level content rules. This packaging defect is identical in both feeds (not introduced by this version) — no delta to flag — but it means this validator run does not confirm content-level checks the way a correctly-packaged feed would.
checks_passed.id_regeneration_required_files: trips 2.2% new IDs (2,568 of 115,254 new, 2,372 removed, 112,686 kept); stops 0.1% (7 of 6,108 new, 2 removed — CE1 & CE2, 6,101 kept); routes 0.2% (1 of 642 new — TTS_461, 1 removed — CE, 641 kept); agency_id / calendar.txt / calendar_dates.txt byte-identical between feeds (no service_id churn at all, no feed_info.txt present in either feed to compare). All well under the 80–90% threshold.
checks_passed.stop_code_change: 3.6% — stop_code changed for 222 of 6,101 common stops, all of which were backfills from empty to a non-empty value (0 cases of an existing non-empty stop_code being changed to a different value); 215 of the 222 exactly match stop_id, 7 are a shortened form (e.g. stop_id 'SKT_A' → stop_code 'A'). Under the >5% threshold and no evidence of stop_code renumbering.
checks_passed.entity_churn: trips +0.2% net (115,058→115,254), stops +0.1% (6,103→6,108), routes 0% (642→642, 1 added/1 removed), shapes +0.02% (151,495→151,530), stop_times +0.1% (3,958,534→3,962,734), transfers -8.8% (68→62, all 6 removed rows tied to the retired CE1/CE2 stops — see suspicious_changes). All well below the 20–50% floor used to flag mass entity loss.
checks_passed.stop_coordinate_drift: 3 of 6,101 common stops moved (CC15, NS17, NS17_CC15 — the Bishan interchange complex), all by the identical 52.0m; the remaining 6,098 common stops are byte-identical on stop_lat/stop_lon. 0 stops moved >100m and 0 moved >500m.
